newsitem.title: USA: Virginia lawmaker to propose property tax repeal.
newsitem.headline: Virginia lawmaker to propose property tax repeal.

text.p: A Virginia lawmaker plans to introduce a bill to eliminate the state's personal property tax when the Virginia General Assembly convenes Wednesday, the Richmond Times-Dispatch said.
The proposal by Sen. Charles Colgan, D-Prince William County, would offset lost revenues by raising the state sales tax to 6 percent from 4.5 percent.
Colgan said the sales tax increase would more than compensate for the $1.1 billion that local governments now raise from the personal property tax on cars, boats and other property.
Critics said the move would hurt areas that do not have large retail outlets, affecting the poor disproportionately.

They also said sales tax revenues were more volatile than property tax revenues, and that the proposal would reduce local autonomy because the state controls sales tax revenues while local governments oversee proprty tax revenues.
Additionally, Gov. Geroge Allen said he would not break his pledge to veto any increase in the sales or state income tax.
Colgan said he previously thought the proposal was a long shot, but that support appears to be growing.
"It might happen, who knows?" Colgan told the Richmond Times-Dispatch.

A poll conducted by Media General Reserach for the newspaper found 57 percent favored raising the sales tax if it meant eliminating the personal property tax. Thirty-three percent said they opposed the plan and 11 percent were undecided or gave no answer. The telephone poll of 406 Richmond-area residents had an error margin of 5 percent.
The poll also found that more than one-fourth of the respondents would be more likely to buy big-ticket items such as cars if the property tax were eliminated.
